source.title: How to Initialize your Network? Robust Initialization for WeightNorm & ResNets
source.authors: Devansh Arpit; Víctor Campos; Yoshua Bengio

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports how initialization and learning-rate warmup affect test error and the performance gap between weight-normalized and batch-normalized networks, a related setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error comparisons and train/test accuracy plots, but does not test random-label memorization or any listed version. Its initialization and Hessian results concern training stability and curvature; cited results about other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization and warmup for weight-normalized networks, not any listed claim version. Its Hessian measurements are at initialization, without magnitude scaling or a measured relationship to generalization gaps; warmup is not evaluated across batch sizes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the proposed initialization improves robustness to depth, hyperparameters, and seed; combined with warmup, it reduces the WN–BN performance difference. The authors connect this to lower curvature at initialization and access to larger learning rates, while acknowledging the remaining WRN-40-10 optimization shortfall.
record.recipe_differences: Studies initialization of weight-normalized networks and compares their test performance with batch-normalized networks; it does not apply the random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization strategy and learning-rate warmup affect training robustness and reported test error; depth and learning-rate choice also affect training success.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposed initialization and warmup reduce WN test errors toward BN results for several residual architectures. WRN-40-10 remains worse and does not fully fit the training set within the epoch budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and learning-rate warmup can reduce performance differences between weight-normalized and batch-normalized residual networks, depending on architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports lower Hessian spectral norms at initialization with the proposed scheme; these measurements do not assess magnitude-aware sharpness of trained solutions or its correlation with generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed initialization places weight-normalized networks in lower-curvature regions that permit larger learning rates.

record.problems: The WRN-40-10 weight-normalized model did not completely fit the training set before the epoch limit. The paper attributes some performance differences to potentially sub-optimal learning-rate schedules. Table 1 reports mean and standard deviation over 5 runs for the weight-normalized methods; BN values are not consistently reported with uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: The table's other initialization conditions are not separately extracted because the selected rows capture the proposed-init versus BN comparisons relevant to the reported gap; no other claim-version results were reported.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on matched image tasks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and batch-dependent recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance in trained networks, its association with train-test gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Generalization performance alone does not test these specific versions. No claim-version results are missing from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
